```{r}
# beginning 

#install.packages(c("dplyr", "janitor"))
library(dplyr)
library(janitor)
linelist_cleaned <- clean_names(linelist_cleaned_cleaned)
names(linelist_cleaned)   # check the result

```

```{r}
#the core dplyr verbs 
#select() - keeps only certain columns
linelist_cleaned_small <- linelist_cleaned %>% select(case_id, patient_age, gender, outcome)
View(linelist_cleaned_small)
#filter - keeps only certain rowns based on a condition
adults <- linelist_cleaned %>% filter(age >= 18)
survivors <- linelist_cleaned %>% filter(outcome == "Recovered")
View(adults)
#mutate() - create or change a column
linelist_cleaned <- linelist_cleaned %>% mutate(age_months = age * 12)
#rename() - rename a specific column 
linelist_cleaned <- linelist_cleaned %>% rename(patient_age = age)
names(linelist_cleaned)
#arrange() - sort rows 
linelist_cleaned %>% arrange(age)          # ascending
linelist_cleaned %>% arrange(desc(age))    # descending
rm(age, patient_id, outcome)
names(linelist_cleaned)
linelist_cleaned %>% arrange(age_years)   # replace with whatever the real column is called
linelist_cleaned <- linelist_cleaned %>% rename(sex = gender)
rm(age, patient_id, outcome)
table(linelist_cleaned$age_unit)
```

```{r}
# chain them together with the pipe 
clean_result <- linelist_cleaned %>%
  clean_names() %>%
  filter(age_years >= 18) %>%
  select(case_id, age_years, sex, outcome) %>%
  arrange(desc(age_years))
names(linelist_cleaned)
head(clean_result)
View(clean_result)
```

```{r}
# count duplicate rows
sum(duplicated(linelist_cleaned))
# remove them
linelist_cleaned <- linelist_cleaned %>% distinct()

#count NAs per column
colSums(is.na(linelist_cleaned))
# see rows with any missing values
linelist_cleaned %>% filter(if_any(everything(), is.na))
```

```{r}
#recording values with case_when() - converts coded/messy values into clean categories.

linelist_cleaned <- linelist_cleaned %>%
  mutate(age_group_simple = case_when(
    age_years < 18            ~ "Child",
    age_years >= 18 & age_years < 65 ~ "Adult",
    age_years >= 65            ~ "Elderly",
    TRUE                        ~ NA_character_   # anything unmatched becomes NA
  ))

table(linelist_cleaned$age_group_simple)

#recording text values - fixing inconsistent categories.
linelist_cleaned <- linelist_cleaned %>%
  mutate(sex = case_when(
    sex %in% c("m", "M", "male", "Male") ~ "Male",
    sex %in% c("f", "F", "female", "Female") ~ "Female",
    TRUE ~ sex   # leave anything else unchanged
  ))

table(linelist_cleaned$sex)

class(linelist_cleaned$date_onset)

install.packages("lubridate")

library(lubridate)   # install.packages("lubridate") if needed

linelist_cleaned <- linelist_cleaned %>%
  mutate(date_onset = ymd(date_onset))  # ymd = year-month-day format
linelist_cleaned <- linelist_cleaned %>%
  mutate(days_to_hospitalisation = date_hospitalisation - date_onset)
summary(linelist_cleaned$days_to_hospitalisation)
View(linelist_cleaned$days_to_hospitalisation)
linelist_cleaned %>% tabyl(sex)
linelist_cleaned %>% tabyl(sex, outcome)
```

```{r}
#working with dates 
install.packages(c("lubridate", "dplyr", "ggplot2"))
library(lubridate)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(rio)
library(here)
linelist_cleaned <- import(here("data", "linelist_cleaneds", "linelist_cleaned_cleaned.xlsx"), which = "Sheet 1")
name(linelist_cleaned)
class(linelist_cleaned$date_onset)
linelist_cleaned <- linelist_cleaned %>%
  mutate(date_onset = ymd(date_onset))    # "2014-05-01" style (year-month-day)

# other common formats:
# dmy("01-05-2014")   # day-month-year
# mdy("05-01-2014")   # month-day-year
today()   # current date
now()     # current date + time
linelist_cleaned <- linelist_cleaned %>%
  mutate(
    onset_year  = year(date_onset),
    onset_month = month(date_onset, label = TRUE),   # gives "Jan", "Feb", etc.
    onset_day   = day(date_onset),
    onset_wday  = wday(date_onset, label = TRUE)      # day of week, e.g. "Mon"
  )
linelist_cleaned <- linelist_cleaned %>%
  mutate(onset_week = floor_date(date_onset, unit = "week"))
names(linelist_cleaned)
linelist_cleaned <- linelist_cleaned %>%
  mutate(days_to_hosp = as.numeric(date_hospitalisation - date_onset))

summary(linelist_cleaned$days_to_hosp)
class(linelist_cleaned$date_onset)
class(linelist_cleaned$date_hospitalisation)
linelist_cleaned <- linelist_cleaned %>%
  mutate(date_hospitalisation = as.Date(date_hospitalisation))
linelist_cleaned <- linelist_cleaned %>%
  mutate(date_onset = as.Date(date_onset))
# now redo the subtraction
linelist_cleaned <- linelist_cleaned %>%
  mutate(days_to_hosp = as.numeric(date_hospitalisation - date_onset))

summary(linelist_cleaned$days_to_hosp)
```
```{r}
#Grouping and summarizing data. group_by(), summarise()
linelist_cleaned %>%
  group_by(outcome) %>%
  summarise(count = n())
#multiple summaries at once.
linelist_cleaned %>%
  group_by(outcome) %>%
  summarise(
    count = n(),
    mean_age = mean(age_years, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_age = median(age_years, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
#grouping by more  than one variable 
linelist_cleaned %>%
  group_by(outcome, gender) %>%
  summarise(count = n())
names(linelist_cleaned)
# count(), a short cut when you just want frequency
linelist_cleaned %>% count(outcome)
linelist_cleaned %>% count(outcome, gender)
# janitor::tabyl()- with % , load janitor first
library(janitor)
linelist_cleaned %>% tabyl(outcome)
linelist_cleaned %>% tabyl(gender, outcome)

#sort by size
linelist_cleaned %>%
  count(hospital) %>%
  arrange(desc(n))
here()
linelist_cleaned <- import(here("data", "linelist_cleaneds", "linelist_cleaned_cleaned.xlsx"), which = "Sheet 1")

#reapplying cleaning steps lost due to restart
linelist_cleaned <- linelist_cleaned %>% clean_names()
linelist_cleaned <- linelist_cleaned %>% rename(sex = gender)

linelist_cleaned <- linelist_cleaned %>%
  mutate(sex = case_when(
    sex %in% c("m", "M", "male", "Male") ~ "Male",
    sex %in% c("f", "F", "female", "Female") ~ "Female",
    TRUE ~ sex
  ))

linelist_cleaned <- linelist_cleaned %>%
  mutate(age_group_simple = case_when(
    age_years < 18 ~ "Child",
    age_years >= 18 & age_years < 65 ~ "Adult",
    age_years >= 65 ~ "Elderly",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_
  ))

linelist_cleaned <- linelist_cleaned %>%
  mutate(date_hospitalisation = as.Date(date_hospitalisation))

linelist_cleaned <- linelist_cleaned %>%
  mutate(days_to_hosp = as.numeric(date_hospitalisation - date_onset))
names(linelist_cleaned)
```

```{r}
#Epidemiological weeks - follow a std numbering system starting Sunday, used for outbreak reporting/surveillance.
linelist_cleaned <- linelist_cleaned %>%
  mutate(epiweek_onset = epiweek(date_onset))
table(linelist_cleaned$epiweek_onset)
format(Sys.Date(), "%d %B %Y")     # "22 September 2026"
format(Sys.Date(), "%B %d, %Y")    # "September 22, 2026"
format(Sys.Date(), "%A, %d %b %y") # "Tuesday, 22 Sep 26"
linelist_cleaned <- linelist_cleaned %>%
  mutate(date_onset_label = format(date_onset, "%d %b %Y"))
linelist_cleaned %>% mutate(test_date = as.Date(41780, origin = "1899-12-30"))
test <- ymd("2014-13-45")   # invalid month/day  that dont respond to a real calender day.
#logially imporsible dates, valid calender dates but nonsensical order - date of hospitilization before symptoms onset.
linelist_cleaned %>%
  filter(date_hospitalisation < date_onset) %>%
  select(case_id, date_onset, date_hospitalisation)
d1 <- ymd("2024-01-01")
d2 <- ymd("2024-03-01")
# durations, periods and intervals - three distint lubridate concepts.
as.duration(d2 - d1)     # exact time elapsed, in seconds (also shows ~weeks)
d2 - years(0) - months(2) - days(0)  # subtracting a "period" - calendar-aware
interval(d1, d2)         # represents the span itself, as a start/end object
my_interval <- interval(ymd("2014-06-01"), ymd("2014-08-31"))
ymd("2014-07-15") %within% my_interval   # TRUE
View(my_interval)

# Epidemic curve,
#aes- aesthetic mapping- tells ggplot the x position, ypos and color/fill
# geom_col() - the shape that actually gets drawn using data from aes, geom_col specifically draws bars whose height comes directly from a value already calculated.
# labs for labels sets the title and axis labels 
library(ggplot2)

linelist_cleaned %>%
  count(epiweek_onset) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = epiweek_onset, y = n)) +
  geom_col() +
  labs(
    title = "Epidemic curve by epidemiological week",
    x = "Epi week",
    y = "Number of cases"
  )
```
